name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,792

entries.clue: Somewhere in Liverpool, puzzling remains ... (6,3)

blocks.note: a knotty problem is a puzzling one
ash is what remains after burning

annotation.surface: An unsolved mystery lingers somewhere in Liverpool, trailing off into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots link this clue to 6 across, which continues the sentence; each still solves on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this suburb in the east of Liverpool was comedian Ken Dodd's lifelong home.

entries.clue: Rescue boat turning up with no good whale carcass (5)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down answer, turning up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

annotation.surface: A lifeboat, upturned, arrives with a worthless whale carcass.
annotation.walkthrough: An obscure word, so the wordplay has to build it letter by letter; the crossings help.
annotation.definitionFit: A whalers' term: the body left once the blubber has been stripped off.

entries.clue: Old hat blooming tatty (7)

blocks.note: flowers that are out are blooming
tatty clothes are worn

annotation.surface: An old hat, flowery but shabby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a literal hat described by 'blooming tatty', with 'blooming' as a mild British intensifier; in fact 'old hat' means outdated.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'old hat' means stale and no longer fashionable.

entries.clue: Freely admit a dumped settee proved useful for ages (4-6)

indicatorNotes.Freely: letters arranged freely can go in any order
indicatorNotes.dumped: the A is dumped, thrown out of the fodder

blocks.note: ADMIT with its A dumped
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone owns up to having fly-tipped an old sofa that served them well for years.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Freely admit' reads as a confession, but 'Freely' is the anagram signal and 'admit' is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: something that has worked over a long period has passed the test of years.

entries.clue: Shift key regularly errs (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the 1st and 3rd of ERRS

blocks.note: the Alt key on a computer keyboard
E and R, the odd letters of ERRS

annotation.surface: A typist complains that the Shift key keeps producing mistakes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shift key' is a real keyboard key, so the eye fuses the two words; the definition is 'Shift' alone and 'key' starts the wordplay with a different key, Alt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to change.

entries.clue: Denied an introduction, men must suppress sighs for Felicity (9)

indicatorNotes.Denied an introduction: the first letter is refused: CHAPS loses its C
indicatorNotes.suppress: HAPS holds PINES down inside it

blocks.note: CHAPS = men, minus the first letter
to pine is to long or sigh for something

annotation.surface: Men are told to hold back their sighs for a woman called Felicity, who snubbed them.
annotation.walkthrough: Felicity looks like a woman's name, capitalised as the first word; here it is the common noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: felicity is a formal word for great joy.

entries.clue: ... altogether popular with advanced students (2,3)

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable, popular
A = advanced, as in A level
L = learner, so two learners are students

annotation.surface: Continuing 1 across: the whole lot is well liked by senior pupils.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 1 across as one sentence; each clue still stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases mean in total, counting everything.

entries.clue: Holly possibly sending up cross priest (4)

indicatorNotes.sending up: in a down answer, sent up means read bottom to top

blocks.note: X is a cross
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, the crossword's favourite priest

annotation.surface: Someone named Holly is mocking an irritated priest.
annotation.walkthrough: Holly looks like a woman's name; 'possibly' warns that the definition is an example rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: holly is one plant of this botanical genus, which also includes the holm oak's namesake.

entries.clue: Lifting Qataris in game to some extent (7)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only part of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of Qataris, through in, to the first letter of game

annotation.surface: Qatari players are rising in a sport, at least partly.
annotation.walkthrough: qat(ARIS IN G)ame: the definition 'Lifting' is at the front, and the rest of the clue is the hiding place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean going up or getting up.

entries.clue: "Plug" in the comic! Take things less seriously (7,2)

indicatorNotes.comic: comic letters are playing the fool, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

annotation.surface: A comic strip character called Plug is urged to relax.
annotation.walkthrough: Plug is a character in The Beano's Bash Street Kids, so 'the comic' reads as the Beano; in fact 'comic' is the anagram signal and 'Plug in the' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrasal verb means relax and stop being so serious.

entries.clue: Party now and then? Given invite, go (7)

indicatorNotes.now and then: take a letter now and then: the 2nd and 4th of PARTY

blocks.note: pArTy, every other letter
to invite trouble is to tempt it

annotation.surface: A casual party-goer, now invited, decides to go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' reads as a verb, leave; as the definition it is a noun, a try, as in 'have a go'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a go at something is a try.

entries.clue: Going about quietly, being a spy (7)

indicatorNotes.about: PEEING goes about, around, the P

blocks.note: to go is a nursery euphemism for to urinate
p = piano, quietly in music

annotation.surface: A spy moves about without a sound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going about quietly' reads as sneaking around; 'Going' is a childish word for relieving oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: looking furtively through a gap is what a spy does.

entries.clue: Fairground Attraction's Perfect finally introduced by presenter wearing weave (5,5)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of Perfect
indicatorNotes.introduced by: T is led in by HOST, which comes before it
indicatorNotes.wearing: GRAIN wears HOST and T, holding them inside

blocks.note: the grain of fabric is the direction of its weave; it goes around the next two pieces
a TV presenter hosts a show
last letter of Perfect

annotation.surface: A pop trivia note: Fairground Attraction's hit 'Perfect' performed by a presenter in a hairpiece.
annotation.walkthrough: Fairground Attraction were a British band whose 1988 number one was 'Perfect', so the surface is about music; the band name is the definition taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a spooky ride through a dark tunnel is a classic funfair attraction.

entries.clue: Former PM's Gulf broadcast (4)

annotation.definitionNote: the possessive 's belongs to the surface; the answer is the name Pitt

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast means spoken on air, so heard, not read

blocks.note: a gulf is a deep pit or chasm

annotation.surface: A news item about an ex-prime minister's policy in the Gulf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gulf' suggests the Persian Gulf and foreign policy; here it is a chasm.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Elder and the Younger were both 18th-century British prime ministers.

entries.clue: First couple in tonight going off syrupy TV film (5-5)

indicatorNotes.First couple in: the first two letters of tonight
indicatorNotes.going off: the letters go off, spoil, and end up scrambled

blocks.note: first two letters of tonight
anagram fodder, eight letters

annotation.surface: A TV guide sniffs that tonight's soppy made-for-TV movie is past its best.
annotation.walkthrough: 'TV film' reads as one phrase, but TV belongs to the anagram and 'film' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Mike Leigh's 1999 film about Gilbert and Sullivan has this title.

entries.clue: Jockeys perhaps wheeze at the end of races (5)

indicatorNotes.at the end of: take the letter at the end of races

blocks.note: to wheeze or pant is to breathe hard
last letter of races

annotation.surface: Jockeys gasp for breath after the finish.
annotation.walkthrough: Jockeys looks like riders; here it is Jockey, a brand of underpants.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Jockey is a brand of men's underwear, and in British English underwear is what this word means.

entries.clue: Chef working to improve turnover? (9)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a restaurant cook worried about the business; the setter means a specialist cook
turnover reads as sales revenue, but a turnover is also a folded fruit pastry, which a pastry chef works to perfect

annotation.surface: A restaurant chef is striving to boost the business's takings.
annotation.walkthrough: Turnover reads as business revenue; the pun is the pastry, a fruit-filled folded pastry, which a pastry chef would improve.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: a pastry chef makes turnovers, not sales figures, better.

entries.clue: Instrument for Rick Wakeman Roger Dean transformed? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.transformed: the letters are changed into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

annotation.surface: A prog rock question: was the Yes keyboardist's instrument reinvented by the band's cover artist?
annotation.walkthrough: Rick Wakeman was the keyboard player of Yes, and Roger Dean painted their album covers, so the two names belong together in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a keyboard instrument sounded by air through reeds suits a keyboard player.

entries.clue: In office again, smirk over application of current journalist (9)

blocks.note: a leer is a nasty smirk
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, applies electric current
ED = editor

annotation.surface: A politician back in power smirks over a journalist given electric shocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as up to date; here it is electric current, and ECT is the medical treatment that applies it.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: winning another vote puts an official back in office.

entries.clue: Cheap flat (9)

blocks.note: cheap as in tacky and vulgar
flat as in bland food or drink

annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheap flat' reads as a bargain apartment; both words are adjectives.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: lacking good judgement in style, and lacking flavour.

entries.clue: Unmentionables? On in 20 seconds! (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so RE sits within SECTS

blocks.note: 20 across is SECT, so 20s is SECTS
re = on, about

annotation.surface: A backstage call: someone's underwear is going on in twenty seconds.
annotation.walkthrough: '20 seconds' is a cross-reference: the answer to 20 across, with 'seconds' pluralising it. Unmentionables is also a coy word for underwear, which the surface uses.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful paraphrase: things you must not mention, with the question mark nodding at the underwear sense.

entries.clue: Peer into kinky porn so right to quit (5)

indicatorNotes.kinky: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order
indicatorNotes.to quit: to quit is to leave, so the R walks out of the fodder before it is rearranged

blocks.note: PORNSO without R
R = right, the letter that quits

annotation.surface: A voyeur peers at some kinky porn, so a respectable person walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram is of PORN SO with the R removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pry, to look into other people's business.

entries.clue: Old beast of burden climbing to get aromatic plant (7)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down answer, climbing reads bottom to top

blocks.note: O = old
an onager is a wild ass

annotation.surface: An old pack animal clambers up to reach a fragrant herb.
annotation.walkthrough: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a fragrant herb of the mint family, used in Italian cooking.

entries.clue: Starters of spicy enchiladas carried to group (4)

indicatorNotes.Starters of: take the starting letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters

annotation.surface: Spicy starters of enchiladas are brought to a table of diners.
annotation.walkthrough: The starters look like food on a menu, but they are initial letters, including those of 'carried to'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a faction or band of people with shared beliefs.

entries.clue: Truss cedes to party charmer? (10)

indicatorNotes.to party: letters sent to party go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

annotation.surface: Politician Liz Truss gives way to a party figure.
annotation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was the shortest-serving British prime minister, so 'Truss cedes to party' reads as politics.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a woman who charms in order to seduce.

entries.clue: Direct and officious librarian in Bow? (5)

indicatorNotes.in Bow: Bow is in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop their H's

blocks.note: direct as in guide someone to a seat
a librarian keeps saying 'hush'; in Cockney speech the H is dropped

annotation.surface: A bossy East End librarian tells people where to go.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow reads as a curtsey or a ribbon; it is a district of London's East End, and Cockney speech drops the H, turning a HUSHER into an 'USHER.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to show people to their places, and a Cockney 'hush-er'.

entries.clue: Joined daughter supporting team (5)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down answer, D sits under SIDE, holding it up

blocks.note: a football side is a team
D = daughter

annotation.surface: A daughter signs up to support a sports team.
annotation.walkthrough: Joined is meant as took sides with, as in 'sided with the rebels'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of allied oneself with a party in a dispute.

entries.clue: Kate perhaps writing about naked pose (4)

indicatorNotes.naked: POSE stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: MS = manuscript, a piece of writing
POSE with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: A model named Kate is photographed in a nude pose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Naked pose' fits the modelling surface exactly, which hides that it only means stripping a word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the supermodel Kate bears this surname.

entries.clue: Kill American snake beginning to terrorise ship (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the beginning letter of terrorise

blocks.note: American slang for murder someone
a boa is a snake
first letter of terrorise

annotation.surface: An instruction to kill a snake before it terrorises a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' tells the solver that this sense of kill is US slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a vessel built to break through ice, or a sailing sled on it.

entries.clue: Getting hold of match official is difficult for Cambridge University (7)

indicatorNotes.Getting hold of: HARD gets hold of VAR, holding it inside

blocks.note: hard = difficult
VAR, the video assistant referee in football

annotation.surface: A match official finds the going tough at Cambridge University.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambridge University looks like the English one; the answer is in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
annotation.definitionFit: A misleading definition by location: the Ivy League university stands in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

entries.clue: Somewhat reflective, impressionist Serafinowicz takes it easy (5)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the letters are used: the answer is inside
indicatorNotes.reflective: a reflection shows the letters back to front

blocks.note: the last two letters of impressionist and first three of Serafinowicz

annotation.surface: A mimic, Peter Serafinowicz, is in a thoughtful mood and relaxes.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter Serafinowicz is a British comic actor known for impressions.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: relaxes, has a break.

entries.clue: I'd try out couch that's blue and disgusting? (5,4)

annotation.definitionNote: a clause describing the noun: something that's blue and disgusting

indicatorNotes.out: the letters of I'D TRY are out of place

blocks.note: anagram fodder
to couch a message is to phrase it

annotation.surface: A shopper tests a sofa, only to find it is a hideous blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Couch looks like a sofa; as a verb it means to put into language. Blue here means rude.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: an obscene term is blue in the sense of rude, and disgusting too.
